title: Malta Year 8 Math — All 19 Chapters: Basic Extended
question: Five more versions of every Basic question: can you do the same step again with new numbers?
intro: **Basic Extended:** 5 more versions of each of the 38 Basic questions, 190 questions in all, grouped by question.

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Car park lift
questions.prompt:
In a Valletta car park, floor 0 is the street.

Floor \(-2\) means 2 floors below the street.

A lift starts on floor \(-2\) and goes up 6 floors.

Which floor does it stop at?
questions.figure_alt: A building with floors −3 to 5 and street level at floor 0. A lift car is on floor −2 and an arrow goes up 6 floors to a floor marked with a question mark.
questions.solution:
Up means add:

\[-2 + 6 = \boxed{4}\]

\(-8\) moves 6 floors down instead of up.

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Kinnie on the table
questions.prompt:
A bottle of Kinnie comes out of the freezer at \(-5\,^\circ\text{C}\) (5 degrees below zero).

On the table it gets 7 degrees warmer.

What is its temperature now?
questions.figure_alt: A thermometer from −6 to 6 °C next to a Kinnie bottle. The start −5 is marked; an arrow goes 7 degrees up to a question mark.
questions.solution:
Warmer means move **up** the thermometer:

\[-5 + 7 = \boxed{2}\]

\(-12\) moves 7 degrees colder instead of warmer; \(12\) forgets the minus sign on \(-5\).

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Diver swims up
questions.prompt:
Sea level is 0 m, and \(-9\) m means 9 m under the water.

A diver at Ċirkewwa is at \(-9\) m.

The diver swims up 5 m.

What is the diver's depth now?
questions.figure_alt: The sea with a depth scale from 0 down to −10 metres. A diver at −9 m; an arrow goes 5 m up to a depth marked with a question mark.
questions.solution:
Up means add:

\[-9 + 5 = \boxed{-4}\]

- The diver is at −4 m.
- \(-14\) swims 5 m deeper instead of up.

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Bank balance
questions.prompt:
A bank balance of −€15 means you owe the bank €15.

Your balance is −€15 and you pay in €40.

What is your balance now?
questions.figure_alt: A number line from −20 to 30 in steps of 5. Start at −15; one jump of 40 to the right lands on a question mark.
questions.solution:
Paying in moves **up** (to the right on the line):

\[-15 + 40 = \boxed{25}\]

- The balance is €25.
- \(55\) adds 15 to 40 and forgets that −€15 is money you owe.

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Rocket countdown
questions.prompt:
A rocket clock counts seconds.

It shows \(-8\), which means 8 seconds before lift-off (lift-off is 0).

Then 11 seconds pass.

What does the clock show now?
questions.figure_alt: A number line from −10 to 5. Start at −8; eleven hops of 1 to the right end at a question mark.
questions.solution:
Time passing moves **right** on the number line:

\[-8 + 11 = \boxed{3}\]

\(19\) adds 8 and 11 and forgets that \(-8\) is before lift-off.

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Colder freezer
questions.prompt:
A freezer is at \(-6\,^\circ\text{C}\) (6 degrees below zero).

You turn it down and it gets 8 degrees colder.

What is the temperature now?
questions.figure_alt: A freezer next to a thermometer from −16 to 4 °C. The start −6 is marked; an arrow goes 8 degrees down to a question mark.
questions.solution:
Colder means move **down** the thermometer:

\[-6 - 8 = \boxed{-14}\]

\(-2\) takes 6 from 8 and forgets that both moves go below zero.

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Hotel lift down
questions.prompt:
In a hotel in St Julian's, floor 0 is the street and floor \(-1\) is 1 floor below it.

A lift starts on floor \(-1\) and goes down 3 floors.

Which floor does it stop at?
questions.figure_alt: A building with floors −5 to 3 and street level at floor 0. A lift car is on floor −1 and an arrow goes down 3 floors to a floor marked with a question mark.
questions.solution:
Down means subtract:

\[-1 - 3 = \boxed{-4}\]

\(2\) moves 3 floors up instead of down.

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Spending in debt
questions.prompt:
Your bank balance is −€20, which means you owe the bank €20.

You spend €15 more with your card.

What is your balance now?
questions.figure_alt: A number line from −40 to 5 in steps of 5. Start at −20; one jump of 15 to the left lands on a question mark.
questions.solution:
Spending moves **left** on the line:

\[-20 - 15 = \boxed{-35}\]

- The balance is −€35.
- \(-5\) adds 15 instead of taking it away.

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Anchor goes down
questions.prompt:

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Quiz points

questions.title: Ch 2 Number Work · Pastizzi boxes
questions.prompt:
A tray has 5 loose pastizzi and 3 boxes with 4 pastizzi in each box.

The total is \(5 + 3\times4\).

questions.figure_alt: Five loose pastizzi plus three boxes with four pastizzi each, then equals a question mark.
questions.solution:
BIDMAS: multiply first (the boxes), then add.

\[3\times4 = 12\]

\[5 + 12 = \boxed{17}\]

\(32\) adds first, as if it were \((5 + 3)\times4\).

questions.title: Ch 2 Number Work · Square patio
questions.prompt:
A square patio is 7 tiles long and 7 tiles wide.

The number of tiles is \(7^2\) (the small 2 means 7 times itself).

How many tiles are there?
questions.figure_alt: A 7 by 7 square of tiles; how many tiles in all is the question.
questions.solution:
A square number is rows times columns:

\[7^2 = 7\times7\]

\[7\times7 = \boxed{49}\]

\(14\) is \(7\times2\), not \(7\times7\).

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · Road junction
questions.prompt:
A side road meets a straight main road.

The two angles at the corner sit on a straight line.

One angle is \(72^\circ\).

Find the other angle.
questions.figure_alt: A straight main road with a side road leaving it. The right angle at the corner is 72°; the left angle is a question mark.
questions.solution:
Angles on a straight line add up to \(180^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 72^\circ = \boxed{108^\circ}\]

\(288^\circ\) uses \(360^\circ\), which is for angles around a point.

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · Ladder on a wall
questions.prompt:
A ladder leans on a wall and stands on flat ground.

On the wall side, the ladder makes \(65^\circ\) with the ground.

Find the angle between the ladder and the ground on the other side.
questions.figure_alt: A ladder leaning on a wall. Between the ladder and the ground on the wall side is 65°; on the other side the angle is a question mark.
questions.solution:
The ground is a straight line, so the two angles add up to \(180^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 65^\circ = \boxed{115^\circ}\]

\(25^\circ\) uses \(90^\circ\), which is for a right angle, not a straight line.

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · Kite string
questions.prompt:
A kite string is tied to a peg on a flat beach at Għajn Tuffieħa.

On one side, the string makes \(40^\circ\) with the sand.

Find the angle between the string and the sand on the other side.
questions.figure_alt: A kite string from a peg on the beach going up to the left. On the left the angle with the sand is 40°; on the right the angle is a question mark.
questions.solution:
The sand is a straight line, so the two angles add up to \(180^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 40^\circ = \boxed{140^\circ}\]

\(320^\circ\) uses \(360^\circ\), which is for angles around a point.

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · Bus ramp

A ramp goes from the flat pavement up to a bus door.

The ramp makes \(20^\circ\) with the pavement on the bus side.

Find the angle between the ramp and the pavement on the other side.
questions.figure_alt: A ramp from the pavement up to a bus door. Between the ramp and the pavement on the bus side is 20°; on the other side the angle is a question mark.
questions.solution:
The pavement is a straight line, so the two angles add up to \(180^\circ\):

\(70^\circ\) uses \(90^\circ\), which is for a right angle, not a straight line.

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · Car park barrier

Find the angle between the arm and the road on the other side.
questions.figure_alt: A red and white barrier arm raised from a post on a straight road. On the left the angle with the road is 55°; on the right the angle is a question mark.

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · Luzzu sail
questions.prompt:
The sail of a luzzu (a Maltese fishing boat) is a triangle.

The mast and the bottom of the sail make a right angle (\(90^\circ\)).

Another corner is \(50^\circ\).

Find the top angle.
questions.figure_alt: A boat with a triangular sail. The corner at the bottom of the mast is a right angle, the far bottom corner is 50°, and the top angle is a question mark.
questions.solution:
The angles in a triangle add up to \(180^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 90^\circ - 50^\circ = \boxed{40^\circ}\]

\(130^\circ\) forgets the right angle and takes only \(50^\circ\) from \(180^\circ\).

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · House roof
questions.prompt:
The roof of a house is a triangle.

The two bottom angles are \(35^\circ\) each.

Find the top angle.
questions.figure_alt: A house with a triangular roof. Both bottom corners of the roof are 35°; the top angle is a question mark.
questions.solution:
The angles in a triangle add up to \(180^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 35^\circ - 35^\circ = \boxed{110^\circ}\]

\(145^\circ\) takes away only one of the two \(35^\circ\) angles.

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · Festa flag
questions.prompt:
A festa flag is a triangle hanging from a string.

The two top angles are \(75^\circ\) each.

Find the angle at the bottom point.
questions.figure_alt: A string of festa flags. The middle flag is a triangle pointing down; its two top angles are 75° and the bottom angle is a question mark.
questions.solution:
The angles in a triangle add up to \(180^\circ\):

\(105^\circ\) takes away only one of the two \(75^\circ\) angles.

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · Triangle park
questions.prompt:
A small park in Sliema is a triangle.

Two of its corners are \(65^\circ\) and \(50^\circ\).

Find the third corner.
questions.figure_alt: A triangular park with trees. Two corners are 65° and 50°; the top corner is a question mark.
questions.solution:
The angles in a triangle add up to \(180^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 65^\circ - 50^\circ = \boxed{65^\circ}\]

\(245^\circ\) takes the angles from \(360^\circ\); a triangle uses \(180^\circ\).

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · Buoy triangle
questions.prompt:
At the Blue Lagoon, a swim route goes round 3 buoys and makes a triangle.

Two of its angles are \(45^\circ\) and \(100^\circ\).

Find the third angle.
questions.figure_alt: A triangle of three buoys in the sea. One angle is 45°, one is 100° and the top angle is a question mark.
questions.solution:
The angles in a triangle add up to \(180^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 45^\circ - 100^\circ = \boxed{35^\circ}\]

\(215^\circ\) takes the angles from \(360^\circ\); a triangle uses \(180^\circ\).

questions.title: Ch 4 Fractions · Birthday cake
questions.prompt:
A round cake is cut into 6 equal slices.

A fraction like \(\frac{1}{6}\) means 1 slice out of the 6.

You eat 2 slices and a friend eats 3 slices.

What fraction of the cake is eaten?
questions.figure_alt: A round cake in 6 slices: 2 orange slices (you), 3 green slices (a friend); the eaten fraction is a question mark.
questions.solution:
Same size slices, so add the tops:

\[\frac{2}{6} + \frac{3}{6} = \boxed{\frac{5}{6}}\]

\(\frac{5}{12}\) adds the bottoms too, but there are still 6 slices, not 12.

questions.figure_alt: A chocolate bar of 12 pieces: 4 orange pieces (you), 3 green pieces (a friend); the eaten fraction is a question mark.
questions.solution:
Same size pieces, so add the tops:

\[\frac{4}{12} + \frac{3}{12} = \boxed{\frac{7}{12}}\]

\(\frac{7}{24}\) adds the bottoms too, but there are still 12 pieces, not 24.

questions.title: Ch 4 Fractions · Cheese pastizzi
questions.prompt:
A tray holds 30 pastizzi.

\(\frac{2}{5}\) of them are cheese pastizzi (\(\frac{2}{5}\) means 2 out of every 5 equal parts).

questions.figure_alt: 30 pastizzi in 5 equal boxes of 6; 2 boxes are shaded and labelled with a question mark.

\[6\times2 = \boxed{12}\]

\(6\) is only one box; you need 2 of the 5 boxes.

questions.title: Ch 5 Decimals · Ftira and Kinnie
questions.prompt:
At a kiosk a ftira costs €3.40 and a Kinnie costs €1.50.

How much do they cost together?
questions.figure_alt: A ftira with a price tag of €3.40 and a Kinnie with a price tag of €1.50; beside them the column sum 3.40 + 1.50 with a question mark for the total.
questions.solution:
Line up the decimal points:

\[3.40 + 1.50 = \boxed{4.90}\]

- The answer is €4.90.
- \(3.55\) puts the 15 in 1.5 under the cents of 3.40 (\(3.40 + 0.15\)) instead of lining up the decimal points.

questions.title: Ch 5 Decimals · Ice cream and water
questions.prompt:
An ice cream costs €2.20 and a bottle of water costs €1.75.

questions.figure_alt: A ice cream with a price tag of €2.20 and a water with a price tag of €1.75; beside them the column sum 2.20 + 1.75 with a question mark for the total.
questions.solution:
Line up the decimal points:

\[2.20 + 1.75 = \boxed{3.95}\]

- The answer is €3.95.
- \(1.97\) writes 2.20 as 0.22 (\(0.22 + 1.75\)) instead of lining up the decimal points.

questions.title: Ch 5 Decimals · Notebook and pen

Line up the decimal points:

\[3.25 + 0.60 = \boxed{3.85}\]

- The answer is €3.85.
- \(3.31\) reads 60 cents as 6 cents (\(3.25 + 0.06\)) instead of lining up the decimal points.

questions.title: Ch 5 Decimals · Ten pastizzi

questions.title: Ch 5 Decimals · Cans of drink

questions.title: Ch 7 Ratio · Football cards
questions.prompt:

questions.title: Ch 7 Ratio · Fruit stall
questions.prompt:

questions.title: Ch 19 Logo · Hexagon rug
questions.prompt:
A robot vacuum cleans around the edge of a rug shaped like a regular hexagon.

Every inside angle is 120°.

The robot vacuum moves forward 15 steps and turns right, 6 times.

In Logo this is `REPEAT 6 [FD 15 RT ?]`.

- `RT ?` means turn right by ? degrees (an angle).

How many degrees is each turn?

questions.solution:
The robot vacuum turns by how much its direction changes:

- Straight on is a turn of \(0^\circ\).
- Turning round to go back is \(180^\circ\).
- The regular hexagon's inside angle is \(120^\circ\), so the turn is

\[180^\circ - 120^\circ = \boxed{60^\circ}\]

Check: 6 turns make one full spin, \(6\times60^\circ = 360^\circ\), so the robot vacuum ends facing up again.

\(120^\circ\) is the inside angle, not the turn: the turn is measured from the dashed straight-on line.

questions.title: Ch 19 Logo · Hexagon flight
questions.prompt:
A drone flies around a garden shaped like a regular hexagon (every inside angle is 120°).

The drone moves forward 20 steps and turns right at each corner, all the way round.

- `RT` means turn right by that many degrees (an angle).

Which commands draw it?
questions.figure_alt: A regular hexagon walked by a drone that starts facing right: arrows 1 to 6 are forward 20 steps each; one inside angle of 120° is marked; at each corner a dashed straight-on line and a right turn marked with a question mark.
questions.solution:
Count the sides and look at one corner:

- The shape has 6 sides, so the commands repeat \(6\) times.
- Straight on (the dashed line) is a turn of \(0^\circ\).
- Turning round to go back is \(180^\circ\).
- The inside angle is \(120^\circ\), so the turn is

\[180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ\]

Check: \(6\times60^\circ = 360^\circ\), one full spin, so the drone is back at the start, facing right.

\[\boxed{\texttt{REPEAT 6 [FD 20 RT 60]}}\]

`REPEAT 6 [FD 20 RT 120]` uses the inside angle: the drone turns the wrong amount, \(6\times120^\circ = 720^\circ\), so it does not draw a regular hexagon. `REPEAT 6 [FD 20 RT 90]` uses the turn for a square: \(6\times90^\circ = 540^\circ\), not one full spin of \(360^\circ\). `REPEAT 3 [FD 20 RT 60]` repeats only 3 times: \(3\times60^\circ = 180^\circ\), less than a full spin, so the shape does not close.
